text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hello! I'm Rowena. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. I'm Ioana.
B: Ioana, lovely. Where are you, love?
A: Burnt Oak. North West London.
B: London! I'm Warrington. What do you do?
A: Lettings admin. Estate agent's.
B: Oh, I could never. All those landlords! Is it stressful?
A: Kind of. It's more the phone calls. The paperwork I don't mind, I actually like that bit.
B: You like paperwork? You need to come and do my inbox, honestly. I'm a nurse, wound care, and I'd rather see ten patients than write one report.
A: [laughs] I'd do your inbox. I wouldn't do the wounds.
B: That's fair! Sorry, I have to ask, I saw the icon on your wall in the photo. Are you Orthodox?
A: Yeah. Romanian Orthodox. My mum's quite religious. I go at Easter and Christmas, mostly for her.
B: I'm Catholic, Filipino Catholic, so I'm at Mass every Sunday, my mum would kill me otherwise, even from the Philippines.
A: [laughs] Yeah, it's like that.
B: Do you like going, though? Or is it just for your mum?
A: Mostly for her. But the Easter one, the midnight service, I do like that. Everyone's holding candles and it's dark and then they sing "Hristos a înviat" and everyone passes the light along. I don't know, it's the one time I actually feel something. Even if I'm knackered.
B: Oh, that gave me goosebumps. We have Simbang A5 at Christmas back home, dawn Masses, nine of them, you get up at four in the morning. Then puto bumbong outside after.
A: Nine? At four?
B: Nine! You get a wish if you do all of them. I never managed it.
A: [laughs] I wouldn't manage one.
B: Did you grow up in London, then?
A: Came at eleven. From Cluj.
B: Eleven, that's a hard age to move.
A: Yeah. It was quite lonely, at school, for a bit. It's fine now.
B: I came at twenty-eight and I still cried for six months, so you did really well. Is your family here?
A: Mum, stepdad, my brother. My grandmother's still in Cluj. I should visit more.
B: Oh, I know that one. My mum and dad are in Batangas. You always think, I should go more.
A: Yeah. Exactly.
B: Sorry, I'm asking you loads of questions, aren't I? I do that.
A: It's fine. You ask normal ones.
B: I'll take that! What's your grandmother's cooking like?
A: Better than mine. Better than my mum's, but don't tell her.
B: [laughs] My lips are sealed.
